messages:
Maya (SRE): Postmortem for the 03:00 UTC throughput spike is live: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-batch-spike. Need to lock SLO edits + assign follow-ups.
Jon P: Quick read. My take: current SLOs aggregate across routes and hide per-route burst behavior. Suggest per-route tail SLOs and tiered SLOs for enterprise customers.
Ellen M: Agree on per-route. Also we should split error budget reporting by customer tier (free/startup/enterprise) so we can prioritize remediation when shared infra causes burn.
Maya (SRE): Proposal draft: 
- Introduce slos:route_p99_9 <= 1200ms with target 99.7% (monthly window)
- Add sustained_throughput SLI: 5m rolling avg >= 90% of baseline (baseline = median weekday 02:00-04:00)
- Error budget policy: classify burns >30%/week for enterprise -> paging; for startups -> alert only.
Jon P: Nice. How do you want to express the p99.9 in PromQL? I'll add to grafana and pager rules.
Maya (SRE): Use this approximate query (per-route):
```
histogram_quantile(0.999, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
```
For the 5m throughput SLI:
```
max_over_time(sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m])) by (route)[5m:1m])
```
Ellen M: I'll own updating the SLO docs and communicating changes to PM/legal for SLA implications. Can we freeze targets until we have 2 weeks of validation data?
Maya (SRE): Yes, validation window = 14 days in staging/production shadow. Only apply to SLAs after PM sign-off.
infra-bot: Detected recurring batch window 02:45-03:15 UTC across 8 customers last 7 days. Pattern ID: batch-2026-03-A.
Jon P: Ops action: add randomized jitter (0-15m) for index jobs and circuit-break to cap concurrent heavy jobs per tenant. I'll open infra change request.
Maya (SRE): Action list (assignments + due dates):
- Jon P: infra change (jitter + tenant concurrency cap) + test in staging (due 2026-03-28)
- Ellen M: SLO doc updates + PM/legal sync for SLA implications (due 2026-03-29)
- Maya (SRE): create dashboard panels for per-route p99.9 and per-tier error budget burn; add monthly SLO review job (due 2026-03-26)
- Ops: add nightly job that flags tenants running >3 heavy jobs during batch window (due 2026-03-30)
Please react with :white_check_mark: if you accept ownership.
Jon P: :white_check_mark: owning infra change.
Ellen M: :white_check_mark: taking docs and comms.
Maya (SRE): infra-bot, can you add runbook steps for mitigations?
runbook-bot: Runbook update queued: add section "Batch window mitigation (02:45-03:15 UTC)" with steps: 1) enable tenant caps, 2) route heavy requests to fallback pool, 3) temporarily scale GPU pool to +20% if sustained P99.9 > 1.2s for >10m.
Jon P: I'll also add a temporary routing policy to prefer preemptible smaller instances for non-enterprise tenants during spikes; will test in staging.
Ellen M: We'll prepare a customer-facing note template in case enterprise SLAs are impacted while we roll changes.
Maya (SRE): I opened a tracking ticket: https://redwood.internal/issues/RED-4310  includes owners/dates. Setting a review meeting next Tue 10:00 to sign off on SLO numbers after the validation window.
Maya (SRE): Final question: do we want to reduce the error budget burn threshold that triggers paging from 30%->20%? Pros/cons?
Jon P: Lower threshold will create noise for infra but gives earlier remediation. Maybe keep 30% for now but add a predictive alert when burn rate slope > X%/day.
Ellen M: Agree with predictive alert. I'll include in the SLO docs.
Maya (SRE): OK, actioned. Meeting invite + reminder set. Thanks all.
